newsitem.title: UK: Treasuries take breather in London after big gains.
newsitem.headline: Treasuries take breather in London after big gains.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries steadied in London on Thursday as European markets were quiet and players decided to take a rest following a recent string of strong gains.
"The stunning rise of prices left a number of participants breathless," said Charles Quigley, vice president at Chase in London.
"We're slightly weaker from Asian prices. There was an initial uptick in volume (in London) and then it subsided pretty quickly with Europe mostly closed."
The long bond at 0957 GMT was at 95-25, to yield 6.960 percent, off from 95-27 in Tokyo and 95-26 in New York.
Long bond yields fell to 6.92 percent on Wednesday, even after strong U.S. gross domestic product data, while two-year note yields dipped to 6.25 percent. That compared with 6.29 percent in London.
Quigley added that prices looked like they had little upside left, at least until after Friday's non-farm payrolls.
The National Association of Purchasing Management report for April is due at 1400 GMT and economists forecast a decline in the index to 53.6 from 55.0.
But only after April payrolls, expected to show a 211,000 rise, are out will people feel comfortable taking big positions again, dealers said.

"We're close enough to unemployment that a lot of players are going to do as little as they have to," Quigley said. Lower than expected labour cost data earlier in the week sparked the recent optimism about the state of the economy.
"We're relatively bullish on the position of the U.S. economy, meaning we don't think it's running away with itself," said Sally Wilkinson, senior economist at Daiwa Europe in London.
"It does seem that slowly the market is turning to the view that perhaps rates aren't going to go up as much as had been anticipated before," she said.
June T-bond futures were at 109-09 in automated trade, unchanged from Wendesday's Chicago settlement.
